$comment: ROOT-TIER RUNNER LEDGER — direction 4 of scripts/audit/ci-pinned-tests-exist.mjs.
A tier config under `vitest/integration/` has exactly two lawful states: a workflow runs it, or it is recorded here.
`slice` is the issue whose work the tier IS — where wiring it belongs. It may be CLOSED, and that is exactly what
this ledger records: the tier shipped and its runner did not. An entry for a tier that IS run, or for a config file
that no longer exists, fails the gate, so this list can only shrink honestly.
The first seven entries below were found by the cinatra#2936 audit; that change wired the four proof tiers of its own plan and left
these untouched, because each belongs to another slice and wiring one needs that slice's services and its judgement.
The eighth entry records the same shape for its own slice, and was added by that slice's own change.

exceptions.reason: No package script reaches this config at all — the only place it is named outside itself is a doc comment in the suite it configures, so there is not even a script for a workflow to call. Wiring it means adding both the script and a step with a real Postgres.
Reached by `pnpm test:usage-ledger`, which no workflow invokes. The tier needs a real Postgres; giving it one is that slice's call, not this CI-wiring change's.
Reached by `pnpm test:unknown-cost`, which no workflow invokes. The tier needs a real Postgres; giving it one is that slice's call, not this CI-wiring change's.
Reached by `pnpm test:week-window`, which no workflow invokes. The tier needs a real Postgres; giving it one is that slice's call, not this CI-wiring change's.
Reached by `pnpm test:install-semantics`, which no workflow invokes. Four suites, a real Postgres and its own provisioning; giving it one is that slice's call, not this CI-wiring change's.
Reached by `pnpm test:durable-reload`, which no workflow invokes — although the issue's own title calls it a required Postgres job. Making it one is that slice's call, not this CI-wiring change's.
Reached by `pnpm test:created-at-immutable`, which no workflow invokes. The tier needs a real Postgres; giving it one is that slice's call, not this CI-wiring change's.

Reached by `pnpm test:loopback-peer`, which no workflow invokes. This tier boots the application's OWN development server and drives it over HTTP, so a runner needs a whole development stack inside one job: a real Postgres, a real Redis (with the queue backend unreachable the boot never reaches ready and the suite's readiness poll simply times out), the per-boot secrets the start-up path refuses to run without, the development runtime mode (the production path needs a baked seed that a plain source-tree run does not produce), the companion extension tree the start-up hook imports, and a ready budget of minutes for a cold compile. One job DOES carry that combination today, the chat-HITL held-turn dev-runtime e2e job, but giving this tier a step there is a workflow change and this change does not make one; that wiring is a CI-wiring change of its own. Folding the suite into a tier that job already runs is not an answer either: each of those configs pins SUPABASE_SCHEMA to a throwaway schema, which the spawned development server would inherit and boot against.
